# God rays

Light shafts that stream from a light past the objects in front of it, as sunbeams through dusty air. The light is a point on screen or a position in the scene.

<EffectDemo effect="god-rays" />

## Usage

```ts
import { EffectComposer } from '@mk7s/xtree/core';
import { godRays } from '@mk7s/xtree/effects/god-rays';

const composer = new EffectComposer(renderer);
composer.setScene(scene, camera);
composer.add(godRays({ preset: 'sunbeams' }));
renderer.setAnimationLoop(() => composer.render());
```

Every parameter is also a property: `effect.position = [0.25, 0.42]`. Uniform changes take effect on the next frame without recompiling.

## Parameters

| Parameter    | Type      | Default             | Range       | Description                                                         |
| ------------ | --------- | ------------------- | ----------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `position`   | [x, y]    | `[0.25, 0.42]`      | -0.5 – 1.5  | Light position on screen (UV), when not following a scene position. |
| `worldLight` | boolean   | `false`             |             | Use a position in the scene for the light instead.                  |
| `lightWorld` | [x, y, z] | `[-2.1, 0.75, 0.4]` | -50 – 50    | Light position in world units, when following the scene.            |
| `intensity`  | number    | `1`                 | 0 – 4       | Brightness of the shafts.                                           |
| `density`    | number    | `0.9`               | 0.1 – 1     | How far toward the light each pixel looks (1 reaches it).           |
| `decay`      | number    | `0.97`              | 0.8 – 1     | How quickly light fades along a shaft.                              |
| `weight`     | number    | `0.01`              | 0.001 – 0.2 | Contribution of each sample.                                        |
| `samples`    | integer   | `48`                | 8 – 128     | Samples per pixel along the shaft.                                  |
| `threshold`  | number    | `1`                 | 0 – 8       | Linear brightness above which pixels cast light.                    |
| `skyWeight`  | number    | `0`                 | 0 – 1       | Light from the far background (sky), besides bright pixels.         |
| `color`      | hex color | `'#fff1d6'`         |             | Color of the light.                                                 |

Every effect also has `blend` (any of the 26 [blend modes](/reference/shaders#modes)), `opacity` (0–1) and `enabled`.

## Presets

| Preset      | Settings                                             |
| ----------- | ---------------------------------------------------- |
| `sunbeams`  | `intensity: 1.5`, `decay: 0.98`, `weight: 0.015`     |
| `tight`     | `density: 0.5`, `decay: 0.95`                        |
| `sky`       | `skyWeight: 1`, `threshold: 3`, `position: [0.5, 1]` |
| `followOrb` | `worldLight: true`                                   |

Apply one with `godRays({ preset: 'name' })` or `effect.applyPreset('name')`; presets start from the defaults.

## Details

- **Family:** Atmosphere & lighting · tracked as story X10.3 in the [plan](https://github.com/s4njee/xtree/blob/main/plan.md).
- **Passes:** samples the pass input at other positions, so it starts a new merged pass; following pixel effects join that pass.
- **Geometry buffers:** reads depth, which the composer renders only while an effect needs them.
- **Masks:** set `effect.mask` to a texture, depth range or selection to limit where it applies; see [masks](/guide/masks).
- **Motion:** Static: nothing animates.
- **Cost:** 339.7 ms added to a 960×540 frame on CI container (SwiftShader software renderer) (2026-10-11). A software renderer: use it to compare effects, not to predict GPU times.
- **Quality tiers:** low: `samples: 20`; medium: `samples: 32`; high keeps the effect's own values. Set `quality`, or leave it `auto` for an [adaptive composer](/guide/performance).
- **Size:** 6.6 KB gzip budget for `@mk7s/xtree/effects/god-rays`, including the shared effect runtime.

Original implementation (MIT). References: Mitchell, Volumetric light scattering as a post-process, GPU Gems 3, ch. 13, 2007.
